definitions.explanation: A firm yellow block of herring eggs, salted or preserved in brine and soaked before eating. It has a distinctive crunch and is a fixture of the New Year's {御節|おせち} box.

examples.japanese: {正月|しょうがつ}には{数|かず}の{子|こ}を{食|た}べる。
examples.english: We eat herring roe at New Year.

examples.japanese: {塩|しお}を{抜|ぬ}いてから{出汁|だし}につけると、{数|かず}の{子|こ}の{歯|は}ごたえが{生|い}きる。
examples.english: Soaking out the salt and then steeping it in dashi brings out the crunch of the herring roe.

notes:
The name comes from {鰊|かど}, an old word for herring: {鰊|かど}の{子|こ} became かずのこ, later written with {数|かず}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {数|かず}の{子|こ}の{塩抜|しおぬ}き: soaking the salt out of herring roe
- {味付|あじつ}け{数|かず}の{子|こ}: pre-seasoned herring roe
- {数|かず}の{子|こ}の{歯|は}ごたえ: the crunch of herring roe

CULTURAL NOTE:
- In the New Year's {御節|おせち} box it stands for fertility and many descendants, since one block holds countless eggs. It sits alongside {黒豆|くろまめ} (black beans, for health) and {田作|たづく}り (candied sardines, for a good harvest) as one of the three classic {祝|いわ}い{肴|ざかな}.
